question.text: Start-up XYZ has 1,00,000 equity shares at INR 10, and Angel Investors hold 30,000 preference shares issued at INR 10 with conversion ratio 1:2 at INR 20/equity. A down round at INR 10/share triggers the angels' Full Ratchet anti-dilution. Under Full Ratchet, the angels will receive a revised equity allocation of:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.6.3 (Anti-Dilution Rights), Full Ratchet resets the conversion price to the lowest issue price (here INR 10). At INR 10/share, 30,000 preference shares convert 1:1 into 30,000 equity shares (vs 15,000 at the original 1:2 ratio based on INR 20). Additional 15,000 shares are issued to the angels. The Trap: 15,000 is the pre-ratchet number. 45,000 and 60,000 apply wrong multipliers unrelated to the ratchet formula. Cross-Exam Context: Same mechanics tested in XIX-A (PE/VC distributor framing); XIX-C tests the Manager's calculation discipline during the down-round negotiation. Manager's Pro-Tip: Full Ratchet is punitive and can sour future investor relations. Weighted-average is the more market-standard approach — only insist on Full Ratchet for pre-Series A seed rounds where you are genuinely subsidizing execution risk.
